name: Marine Diesel Engine
tagline: Independent marine diesel information for Australia
description: Independent Australian guides to marine diesel engines, faults, service costs and how to find a marine mechanic. We do not sell repairs.
_comment_publishing: defaultAuthor is the publishing organisation and is a legitimate byline. defaultReviewer must be a real, named marine mechanic whose review can be substantiated — never a placeholder, nickname or unrelated business. Leave it null until that person has reviewed the material.
defaultAuthor: The Marine Diesel Engine editorial team
_comment_domain: Must match the host actually served. The apex 308-redirects to www in production, so canonicals, Open Graph URLs and every sitemap entry use www — otherwise each one costs a redirect hop and the canonical points at a URL that is not the one served.
_comment_staticRoutes: Pages built from .astro rather than content/. They are real URLs and must appear in the sitemap — the homepage is the most important URL on the site and was previously absent from it entirely.

heroFigure.alt: Compact inboard marine diesel engine installed in a yacht engine bay, with the alternator, drive belt, coolant reservoir, hoses and raw-water strainer visible.
heroFigure.caption: Know what you are looking at before you start troubleshooting. Our guides explain the systems around the engine as well as the engine itself.

_comment_heroFigure: Set to {src, alt, caption} to show a figure under the homepage hero. src must be a file in public/ — prebuild-check enforces that, because a hero that 404s is worse than no hero. alt should describe the useful visual details for search engines and screen readers.
_comment_contact: Used on the privacy and terms pages. Point this at a mailbox that is actually monitored — both pages invite corrections and listing removal requests, and the privacy page commits to responding.
